Reference / os/command

os/command#

Commanding is the immutable description accepted by process consumers.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let status is Commanding = Command(
    program: Path("/usr/bin/git"),
    arguments: ["status", "--short"],
    environment: environment,
    directory: repository,
);

Description#

Commanding is the immutable description accepted by process consumers. It never invokes a shell: every argument remains one exact string.

Command retains a completely explicit execution context. A Path containing a directory component selects that executable directly. A bare Path such as Path("git") asks the runtime to search PATH from this command's Environment:

InheritedCommand deliberately observes the process environment and working directory through its corresponding actions. Its constructor only retains the program and arguments:

let version is Commanding = InheritedCommand(
    program: Path("/usr/bin/git"),
    arguments: ["--version"],
);

Use Path("git") to search PATH from the command's own Environment. The runtime performs direct process lookup; no shell parses the name or args.

string() is diagnostic and never shell-round-trippable. It omits the environment, but arguments themselves can still contain secrets.
